the product's classification codes under the selected node of any level
The item project (`AD_CODPROJ`, labeled *setor* by the reference) differs from the note project (`CAB.CODPROJ`) on most items; restrictions use the item project the reference reports. Other dimensions found during discovery (partner, operation type, financial nature, lot buyer) are not offered: they either duplicate a seller restriction, carry no business meaning for consultation, or have no verified relationship to sale rows.
Every restricted result records its value-only scope and starts its warnings with "Resultado limitado ao seu acesso (code): …. Não é o total da fonte." History and evidence are shown and reused only while the reader's current scope covers that recorded scope; figures computed before a restriction existed are treated as unrestricted. A semantic product selection that names VR Master buyers outside the person's buyer restriction is refused with the permission and the values to release; other selections run with the restriction applied.

title: Sales Capability
heading: Identity, privacy, and context
text:
Identity, privacy, and context
Sales execution requires the source's sales permission, with its current data restriction computed by identity ([access and restrictions](#access-and-restrictions)), under Orion's verified bearer principal, or explicit local access. The [agent](corporate-agent.md#persistent-conversations-and-context) owns durable conversation identity, concurrency, context and history. Sales context stores structured conversation state (last executed plan and query, unanswered request, bounded exchanges with application-authored replies); ERP result rows are not model context. The context does not depend on the source. The legacy `/sales/chat` endpoint always uses Sankhya. Failed turns preserve prior filters. The legacy sales endpoints keep their original 30-minute/12-question in-memory semantics for compatibility, while the product exclusively uses durable agent endpoints.
The explicit `IA_MNS_LOCAL_ACCESS=true` mode is for a single developer on loopback only. Configuration rejects it in production or on a public listener; requests also require a loopback client/host, a local browser origin, and the custom client header, and reject cross-site fetches. It grants the local developer the sales-read capability. Do not expose the development Vite proxy or tunnel it; local mode is not a shared environment authentication system. Production requires configured providers and a trusted verifier at startup. A concrete issuer/login remains conditional under PJ-05.
Sales, questions, filters, and product descriptions are CONFIDENTIAL. Credentials are RESTRICTED. The browser holds token/context/results in memory and clears them on credential changes; only the light/dark theme preference uses browser storage. Protected responses use no-store. New conversation preserves history; explicit deletion removes persisted conversation/context/turns. Model requests use `store:false`, which does not establish zero provider retention or account-specific policy. Only questions and filter context go to OpenAI, never sales rows, prices, customer names, credentials, or raw schema. Users must avoid putting unrelated confidential information or credentials in questions.
Provider exceptions produce safe public error envelopes plus one correlated, allowlisted diagnostic, including the provider/stage and bounded public Oracle/OpenAI error codes. Provider/stage remain internal and never include raw messages or configuration. Rollback/close failures remain provider failures and prevent returning an unverified success. No prompt, result, query binds, Oracle connect descriptor, VRMaster host or account, or secret enters logs. Chat input is limited to 2,000 characters and 12 KB transport size; actor rate limit is 15 questions per minute. Model timeout is 20 seconds, Oracle round-trip timeout 45 seconds, pool wait 5 seconds, and execution deadline 90 seconds. VRMaster statements stop after 30 seconds (the account's own limit, repeated in the transaction), locks after 5 seconds, the client gives up after 35 seconds, connections after 5 seconds, and an aborted turn ends its connection. With `Tudo`, both sources run in parallel within the same deadline. Agent acceptance returns immediately and its browser polls actual progress. The legacy sales route overrides the foundation socket inactivity timeout to 95 seconds, while other routes retain their existing budget. Real ERP queries exceeded the original 10-second round-trip limit, so the bounded budgets now accommodate the measured workload. Limits are process-local, not a distributed quota.

title: Sales Capability
heading: Local execution and external verification
text:
Local execution and external verification
Follow [setup](../setup.md#sales-chat) and the generated [configuration reference](../generated/configuration/api.md). Oracle node-oracledb 7 supports Oracle 12.1 in Thin mode; if an actual authentication/network feature requires Thick mode, configure a compatible Oracle Client directory. Client 19 or 21 supports this database version; newer clients are not automatically compatible with older servers ([driver compatibility matrix](https://node-oracledb.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user_guide/installation.html)). The account must have CREATE SESSION and SELECT only on the reference tables, with schema resolution supplied by the DBA. No login/provider or real ERP account is provisioned by this repository.
The 2026-10-01 read-only audit connected to Oracle 12.1.0.2 with Client 19.32 after the configured Client 11.2 failed with DPI-1050 and Thin mode failed with NJS-116. Nine structured-query scenarios matched the supplied SQL's aggregates in a shared read-only snapshot: monthly net value, month to date, rolling 30-day weight, quantity by unit, product breakdown, previous year, equal-length prior period, accent/case equivalence, and no matching sales. The complete 46-column reference projection also matched for the current three-month product scope. Returns and bonus movements were present in the source and excluded by the final sales filter. Actual HTTP injection with the real Oracle adapter passed annual comparison and empty-result handling using a controlled planner; this is not a live natural-language test.
The audit exposed unrelated description-prefix matches, a comparison product list exceeding the original cap, and Oracle work exceeding the original timeout. Word boundaries now exclude unrelated prefixes, both periods contribute to the product list, limits reject truncation, and eligible-control pruning reduces work while retaining the reference projection. Oracle response shape/numeric checks reject malformed results rather than inventing empty sales. Small fetch batches in this legacy Oracle/Thick stack produced an intermittent difference in one complete record, although database-side MINUS in both directions returned no differences and aggregates matched. Fetching the complete bounded result together matched every field; the adapter now aligns its fetch array size with each result cap. This workaround does not establish the precise driver/server cause, which remains a DBA investigation under PH-08.
No business totals, credentials, or connection descriptor are committed as evidence. The owner later configured a key manually and explicitly authorized reuse. Ten actual language requests, eight original-SQL reconciliations, and a real-browser sales query passed; see [live verification](../project/live-sales-verification.md). Synthetic tests remain distinct evidence. The supplied account also has broad write privileges, which the DBA must remove by providing a dedicated reader. Weight-unit and currency confirmation remain owner actions.
Boundary tests use the real OpenAI SDK with synthetic HTTP responses and Oracle connection doubles. API injection tests exercise actual Fastify authorization, context, validation, and error envelopes. Browser journeys exercise the generated SDK with intercepted synthetic sales responses, while the unavailable-configuration path reaches the real emitted API. These checks do not replace validation against Oracle 12.1 or a live model. Run the full [validation gate](../validation.md) before handoff. On the real ERP, compare at least an adjusted item, a bonus exclusion, a return exclusion, multiple adjustment joins, accented descriptions, mixed units, missing weight, month end, and both comparison periods against the reference. No verification operation writes ERP data.

title: Sales Capability
heading: VRMaster
text:
VRMaster
Set the `VRMASTER_DB_*` settings of the [setup](../setup.md#sales-chat) with the dedicated read-only account of [PH-19](../project/human-actions.md#ph-19) (`CONNECT`, `USAGE` on `public`, `SELECT` only on the nine reference tables, `default_transaction_read_only = on`, 30-second statement timeout); never the PDT Connect account. On 2026-10-07 the VRMaster server answered the PostgreSQL TLS request negatively, so its connection needs `VRMASTER_DB_SSL_MODE=disable`, which sends the credentials and sales data unencrypted on that network; the default `verify-full` refuses to connect without TLS. Without VRMaster settings, selecting it reports the source as not configured.
The adapter's tests run the fixed SQL on PostgreSQL 16 with a synthetic VRMaster schema and the PH-19 grants: period totals and inclusive dates, monthly and product grouping, accent- and case-insensitive whole-word product phrases, comparisons, packaging-type quantities, every reference join (excluded and included rows), bound text that looks like SQL or a regular expression, no transaction left open, cancellation of a blocked read and unavailable or refused connections. They establish the transcription's behavior, not agreement with the real VRMaster; that is the reconciliation of [PH-20](../project/human-actions.md#ph-20), with the queries in [VRMaster reconciliation](../project/vrmaster-reconciliation.md).

title: Sankhya Product Lookup
heading: Availability and scope
text:
Availability and scope
The adapter identifies physical `TGFPRO` registrations through the existing `products` capability and the SNK-PRD-01 permission (`products_sankhya:read`). Choose **MNS (Sankhya)** in the source selector. When both adapters are configured, **Tudo** asks for one ERP: product codes, selections and pending choices remain independent. It does not calculate sales, quantities, conversion factors, prices, stock, legal certificate validity or availability by company.
The configured privileged account is authorized for local discovery only. The runtime refuses ERP object owners and accounts with privileges beyond CREATE SESSION and object SELECT, before executing product queries. The subsequent [owner-authorized provisioning](../project/runtime-access-verification.md) granted the existing `IA_MNS_RO` account its minimum access and verified Runtime execution; PH-08 retains business confirmations. No ERP grants, writes, migrations or procedures were executed. The later [ERP access decision](../security/erp-database-access.md) separates administrative Discovery credential delivery from runtime; actual Runtime grant verification is recorded separately.

title: Sankhya Product Lookup
heading: Dictionary and physical discovery
text:
Dictionary and physical discovery
The [official Data Dictionary documentation](https://developer.sankhya.com.br/docs/dicion%C3%A1rio-de-dados) describes the entity mappings, relationship expressions, calculated fields and properties that must accompany physical metadata. Read-only Oracle discovery on 2026-10-11 reconciled:
Structure
Captured knowledge
`TDDTAB`
Physical table names and business descriptions
`TDDCAM`
Field names, descriptions, calculated/custom flags and expression fingerprints
`TDDINS`
Instance ids/names, inheritance, active state, expression fingerprints and key-script presence
`TDDLIG`
Origin/target instances, direction, mandatory flag, relationship/instance-rule fingerprints
`TDDLGC`
Every mapped field pair, including composite keys
`TDDOPC`
Stored values and descriptive labels, joined through field ids
`TDDPCO`
Additional property names and value fingerprints, including possible interceptors/security rules
Oracle native catalogs
Actual column types/nullability, PK/unique/FK column positions and enabled/validated status, indexes and local synonym resolution
`TGFPRO` has 444 physical columns, 412 dictionary fields and ten custom dictionary fields. Four dictionary fields are calculated (including `TIPO`); none are used by runtime projections. Product-table metadata describes 22 instances and 160 outgoing instance relationships, 63 of which carry relationship/target expressions, conditions or key scripts requiring separate review. The bounded product frontier covers 11 tables, 928 physical columns and 267 outgoing dictionary relationships. The snapshot preserves edges beyond the frontier as discovered candidates; it does not expose them as executable joins. Related tables are `TGFGRU`, `TGFMAR`, `TGFVOL`, `TGFVOA`, `TGFPAP`, `TGFPAR`, `TGFCLP`, `TGFCLA`, `TSICUS` and custom `AD_LISTADCEMB`. The frontier was selected from actual product mappings and relevant two-hop paths; synchronization does not crawl the entire ERP or automatically expand this reviewed scope.
Dictionary expressions, BeanShell, UI reference parameters and key scripts are never executed. Raw expressions/property values are fingerprinted rather than included in the tracked snapshot or model prompt. Metadata contains no ERP product/partner rows, credentials, connection descriptors or database-owner names.

title: Sankhya Product Lookup
heading: Physical registration and JAPE instances
text:
Physical registration and JAPE instances
`Produto` is instance 27, with a dynamic `TSIPAR`-dependent `SERVFILUSOPROD` expression governing service usage `S` and excluding usage `3`; `Servico` is a separate instance (29). Product instance descendants inherit additional rules. These are entity semantics, not unconditional SQL relationships. The adapter explicitly queries physical `TGFPRO`, including services/tariffs, and explains that scope in every answer. It does not claim parity with JAPE `Produto`.
`USOPROD` has 15 descriptive options in `TDDOPC`. Actual registrations also contain `S` (107 rows) and `3` (seven rows), without descriptive options there. Those codes remain included in an unrestricted physical registration query, but are not invented as named domain filters. Complete dictionary option labels take precedence over qualified partial matches; multiple remaining matches require clarification.

title: Sankhya Product Lookup
heading: Verified relationship graph
text:
Verified relationship graph
Every executable edge records source/destination, all join pairs, conditions, cardinality, meaning, dated evidence, dictionary instance ids, physical constraint and confidence in the catalog. The following edges have high confidence for physical joins; dictionary/JAPE rules are assessed separately.
Path from product
Join and cardinality
Verified evidence and interpretation
Group
`TGFPRO.CODGRUPOPROD → TGFGRU.CODGRUPOPROD`, many-to-one
Every one of 10,959 products has a valid group; FK and instance mapping agree
Group ancestors
`TGFGRU.CODGRUPAI → CODGRUPOPROD`
672 nodes, maximum depth three; explicit parent ids, including negative root sentinel and special group zero; no numeric prefix assumption
Registered brand
`CODMARCA → TGFMAR.CODIGO`, many-to-one
All non-null values reference unique brands; 100 assigned brand ids, distinct from 114 free-text `MARCA` values
Base / purchase unit
`CODVOL` / `CODVOLCOMPRA → TGFVOL.CODVOL`, many-to-one
Enabled validated FKs; string key `VARCHAR2(2)`; purchase unit may be absent
Alternate unit
`CODPROD → TGFVOA.CODPROD → TGFVOL.CODVOL`, one-to-many then many-to-one
18,185 rows cover 4,909 products; composite registration PK `(CODPROD,CODVOL,CONTROLE)`
Linked supplier
`CODPROD → TGFPAP.CODPROD`, then `CODPARC → TGFPAR.CODPARC`
8,956 registrations cover 3,746 products; link PK `(CODPARC,CODPROD,SEQUENCIA)`; explicit `FORNECEDOR='S'` condition enforces supplier meaning
Additional classification
`CODPROD → TGFCLP → TGFCLA.CODCLASSIF`
Physical FKs and mapped pairs agree, but both tables are empty; dimension disabled pending nonempty validation
Custom packaging list
Product → group, `TGFGRU.AD_CODLISTADC → AD_LISTADCEMB.CODLISTA`
Custom FK and mapped pairs agree; 300 groups assign seven nonzero lists; immediate-group assignment only
The product-to-alternate-unit and product-to-partner-link mappings carry the reviewed `@ref-param[include-in-deep-copy=true]` annotation. Only its exact known fingerprint is accepted as a harmless copy annotation. Arbitrary relationship expressions cannot enter compilation. The preferred-supplier instance instead carries a supplier expression; it is not silently promoted to a general join.
The group parent graph is validated for duplicate keys, cycles, missing positive parents and depth above eight. Oracle traverses explicit parents with `CONNECT BY NOCYCLE`, also bounded to eight. Source nodes carry their actual ancestor ids so the shared resolver can compare containment without ERP-specific arithmetic. Composite bridge registrations retain every mapped join pair; named-value lookup currently requires a single key.

title: Sankhya Product Lookup
heading: Filtering capabilities
text:
Filtering capabilities
Enabled dimension
Meaning and limitations
Group / category
Named group and descendants; candidate discovery also uses product descriptions and synonyms
Registered brand
`CODMARCA` registration; free-text brand is not substituted
Base unit
Main registered unit; KG does not imply the VR Master weighable flag
Purchase unit
Purchase unit on the current product registration
Alternate unit
Any registered alternate unit, active or inactive; no conversion or control selection
Linked supplier
Product-partner association with supplier role; neither preferred supplier nor purchase history
Product usage
Only descriptive options found in the official dictionary
Active
Current product `ATIVO='S'`; no company/store availability inference
Description
Literal whole-word text, case/accent insensitive
Characteristics
Literal text in `CARACTERISTICAS`, populated on 306 products; independent of description
EPI certificate
Literal additional field `AD_CA`, dictionary description CA E.P.I., populated on 26 products
Additional-packaging list
Custom list assigned directly to the immediate group; no inherited pricing or discounts
Filters combine through the shared validated selection AST, with null-safe exclusions and nested `EXISTS` for one-to-many paths. Products are never multiplied by alternative-unit or supplier registrations. Supplier candidate retrieval enforces the same supplier-role predicate as final execution. Supplier values may identify natural persons; candidate names stay out of model input and are resolved through the existing deterministic choice mechanism.
Not established: buyer responsibility, manufacturer, meaningful cost-center classification, preferred supplier, additional classification on nonempty data, computed fields, company-dependent instance rules, barcode selection, packaging conversion and inheritance. `CODPARCFORN` and product `CODCENCUS` contain only zero, `CODFAB` is empty, and custom `AD_CODUSU` identifies the last editing user, not a buyer. Names alone are insufficient evidence. No relationship was invented to satisfy these questions.
